title: Neonatal Jaundice: Physiologic Versus Pathologic Features
subject: Pediatrics
preview: Newborn jaundice requires interpretation by age in hours, gestation, bilirubin level and risk factors.
quickRevision: Newborn jaundice requires interpretation by age in hours, gestation, bilirubin level and risk factors.
Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia can cause bilirubin neurotoxicity when severe; conjugated jaundice suggests other pathology.
Use age- and risk-specific nomograms or approved guidance for phototherapy decisions.

sections.title: Clinical syndrome and red flags
points: Newborn jaundice requires interpretation by age in hours, gestation, bilirubin level and risk factors.
Jaundice within the first day of life is concerning and needs prompt assessment.

sections.title: Differentiate and manage
points: Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia can cause bilirubin neurotoxicity when severe; conjugated jaundice suggests other pathology.
Use age- and risk-specific nomograms or approved guidance for phototherapy decisions.

sections.title: Memory aid
points: Neonatal jaundice red flags: unusually early onset, fast progression, illness, poor feeding and prolonged jaundice.
Always interpret bilirubin against the infant’s age, gestation and risk factors rather than one universal threshold.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not decide treatment from a bilirubin number without age in hours and gestation.

quiz.question: Which timing of neonatal jaundice is particularly concerning?
options: Later mild physiologic onset in an otherwise well term infant
quiz.explanation: Onset during the first 24 hours. Neonatal jaundice red flags: unusually early onset, fast progression, illness, poor feeding and prolonged jaundice.
